info.title: Manus OpenAPI v2
info.description: API for integrating Manus into your workflow. All responses are wrapped with {"ok": true, "request_id": "...", ...} for success and {"ok": false, "request_id": "...", "error": {"code": "...", "message": "..."}} for errors.

get.description: Returns the Manus user ID associated with the authenticated API key or OAuth2 access token. This endpoint is read-only and does not require an OAuth scope.

request_id.description: Unique identifier for this API request.

user_id.description: Manus user ID associated with the authenticated credential.

parameters.name: x-manus-api-key
parameters.description: API key for direct authentication. Provide either this or `Authorization`, not both. See [Authentication](https://open.manus.ai/docs/v2/authentication).

parameters.name: Authorization
parameters.description: OAuth2 access token in `Bearer {token}` format. No OAuth scope is required. Provide either this or `x-manus-api-key`, not both. See the [Open App](https://open.manus.ai/docs/v2/open-app) guide.

post.description: Creates a new task. The task runs asynchronously. Poll for progress with [task.listMessages](https://open.manus.ai/docs/v2/task.listMessages), send follow-ups with [task.sendMessage](https://open.manus.ai/docs/v2/task.sendMessage). See the [Task Lifecycle](https://open.manus.ai/docs/v2/task-lifecycle) guide for the complete flow.

message.description: The message to start the task with. Contains the prompt text, optional file attachments, and connector/skill configuration.

project_id.description: Project ID to associate this task with. The project's instruction will be automatically applied. Use [project.list](https://open.manus.ai/docs/v2/project.list) to get available project IDs.

locale.description: Locale for the task output language (e.g., "en", "zh-CN", "ja"). Defaults to the user's account locale setting.

interactive_mode.description: When enabled, the agent may pause and ask follow-up questions if the input is insufficient. When disabled (default), the agent proceeds with best-effort execution without asking.

hide_in_task_list.description: When true, the task does not appear in the Manus webapp task list. It remains accessible through the `task_url` in the response.

share_visibility.description:
Who can view the task.

- `private` (default) — only the task creator.
- `team` — all team members.
- `public` — anyone with the `share_url`, without authentication.

agent_profile.description: Agent profile to use for the task. Use the stable values `standard` (default), `lite`, or `max`. For `max`, you can also choose a thinking level with `max-medium`, `max-high`, `max-extra`, or `max-ultra` (deepest reasoning, slowest, and highest credit usage); plain `max` uses the default Max thinking level, currently equivalent to `max-extra`. Versioned aliases such as `1.6-lite`, `2.0-max`, `2.0-max-ultra`, and the legacy `manus-1.6-lite` form are also accepted; the version segment is ignored because model versions are not selected independently. A version without a suffix, such as `1.6` or `manus-1.6`, means `standard`. Omit the field (or pass an empty string) to use `standard`. Free personal accounts are downgraded to `lite` regardless of the requested value.

title.description: Custom title for the task. If not provided, a title will be auto-generated based on the input message.

structured_output_schema.description: JSON Schema for structured output extraction. When provided, the agent runs normally, then a post-processing step extracts a result conforming to your schema. The schema must follow the [Structured Output](https://open.manus.ai/docs/v2/structured-output) subset of JSON Schema: all object properties must be listed in `required`, and `additionalProperties` must be `false`. See the [Structured Output](https://open.manus.ai/docs/v2/structured-output) guide.

request_id.description: Unique identifier for this API request, useful for debugging.

task_id.description: Unique identifier for the created task. Use this to track, update, or delete the task.

task_title.description: Title for the task. Returns the custom title if one was provided in the request, otherwise an auto-generated title based on the input message.

task_url.description: URL to view the task in the Manus webapp (e.g., https://manus.im/app/{task_id}).

share_url.description: Publicly accessible URL for sharing. Only present when share_visibility is not "private".

share_visibility.description: The actual visibility state of the task.

package main

	"io"

func main() {

	url := "https://api.manus.ai/v2/task.detail?task_id=<string>"

post.description: Sends a follow-up message to a task for multi-turn conversation. Use this after [task.create](https://open.manus.ai/docs/v2/task.create) to continue talking, or to answer `messageAskUser` / `cascadeAskUser` questions with ordinary message.content. For supported action confirmations, review confirm_input_schema and the target tool event, then use [task.confirmAction](https://open.manus.ai/docs/v2/task.confirmAction). Do not automatically confirm unrecognized waiting types.

task_id.description: The unique identifier of the task to send the message to. Supports the shortcut `agent-default-main_task` for the IM agent's main task.

message.description: The follow-up message. Supports the same content formats as task.create (plain text or multi-part with files). Note: `message.connectors` behaves differently here than in task.create — a non-empty list overrides the task's connectors, while omitting it (or passing an empty array) reuses the connectors configured at task.create time rather than re-resolving project/user defaults. To remove all connectors, use the top-level `clear_connectors` field instead.

agent_profile.description: Agent profile override for this turn and subsequent turns. Use the stable values `standard`, `lite`, or `max`, or a Max thinking level: `max-medium`, `max-high`, `max-extra`, or `max-ultra`. The thinking level also applies to subsequent turns; plain `max` keeps the level the task already uses; a task that has never selected a level uses the default, currently equivalent to `max-extra`. Versioned aliases such as `1.6-lite`, `2.0-max`, `2.0-max-ultra`, and the legacy `manus-1.6-lite` form are also accepted; the version segment is ignored because model versions are not selected independently. A version without a suffix, such as `1.6` or `manus-1.6`, means `standard`. Omit the field (or pass an empty string) to keep the task's current profile and thinking level; unlike [task.create](https://open.manus.ai/docs/v2/task.create), this endpoint does not default to `standard`. Free personal accounts are downgraded to `lite` when an override is provided.

structured_output_schema.description:
JSON Schema for structured output extraction, armed for the next time this task finishes (`stop_reason: finish`).

- A new schema replaces any previous one.
- Omitted — the current schema state is unchanged; an armed schema is not cleared.

See the [Structured Output](https://open.manus.ai/docs/v2/structured-output) guide.

clear_connectors.description: Removes all connectors from this task for this and subsequent turns. Combine with `message.connectors` to form three states: a non-empty `message.connectors` **overrides** the task's connectors with the new list; `clear_connectors: true` **clears** all connectors; omitting both **reuses** the connectors configured at task.create time. Passing a non-empty `message.connectors` together with `clear_connectors: true` is a conflict and returns `InvalidArgument`.

200.description: Message sent successfully. The task will resume processing.

request_id.description: Unique identifier for this API request.

task_id.description: The ID of the task the message was sent to.

published_version_id.description: **Optional.** `version_id` of the checkpoint currently published. Present only when the site has been published. Match against `data[].version_id` to find the live checkpoint.

post.description: Deploys the latest checkpoint of a website and sets its visibility. Deployment is asynchronous — poll [website.status](https://open.manus.ai/docs/v2/website.status) until `publish_status` becomes `published` or `failed`. To change metadata (title, visibility) without redeploying, use [website.update](https://open.manus.ai/docs/v2/website.update) instead. See the [Website](https://open.manus.ai/docs/v2/website) guide.

task_id.description: Session UID. Mutually exclusive with `website_id` — exactly one must be provided.

website_id.description: Unique website ID. Mutually exclusive with `task_id` — exactly one must be provided.

visibility.description:
Who can access the published site. Replaces the site's current visibility.

- `public` (default) — anyone. An empty string also means `public`.
- `team` — current team members only. Requires a team account.
- `private` — owner and invited collaborators only.

Sites may cap the maximum allowed visibility; requests above the cap return `403 permission_denied`.

200.description: Publish triggered successfully. The response includes the website title current when the request was accepted. Deployment is still in progress — poll `website.status` for the final state and effective visibility. This response does not echo `visibility`.

request_id.description: Unique identifier for this API request.

title.description: Display title of the website when the publish request was accepted. For historical websites without a stored title, this falls back to the internal project name. Always present.

version_id.description: `version_id` of the checkpoint being deployed — always the latest checkpoint of the site.

parameters.name: x-manus-api-key
parameters.description: API key for direct authentication. Provide either this or `Authorization`, not both. See [Authentication](https://open.manus.ai/docs/v2/authentication).

parameters.name: Authorization
parameters.description: OAuth2 access token in `Bearer {token}` format. No OAuth scope is required. Provide either this or `x-manus-api-key`, not both. See the [Open App](https://open.manus.ai/docs/v2/open-app) guide.

post.description: Updates website configuration without deploying. Omitted fields are unchanged; a request with no updatable field returns `400 invalid_argument`. Use [website.publish](https://open.manus.ai/docs/v2/website.publish) to deploy a new version. See the [Website](https://open.manus.ai/docs/v2/website) guide.

task_id.description: Session UID. Mutually exclusive with `website_id` — exactly one must be provided.

website_id.description: Unique website ID. Mutually exclusive with `task_id` — exactly one must be provided.

title.description: New title for the website. Omit to leave unchanged; an empty string is invalid.

visibility.description:
New visibility. Omit to leave unchanged; an empty string is invalid.

- `public` — anyone.
- `team` — current team members only. Requires a team account.
- `private` — owner and invited collaborators only.

The same visibility caps as `website.publish` apply.

auto_publish.description: Optional. Enable or disable automatic publishing for new checkpoints. Automatic publishing preserves the website's current visibility. Omit to leave unchanged; changing this setting does not publish existing checkpoints or cancel an in-flight deployment.

request_id.description: Unique identifier for this API request.

parameters.name: x-manus-api-key
parameters.description: API key for direct authentication. Provide either this or `Authorization`, not both. See [Authentication](https://open.manus.ai/docs/v2/authentication).

parameters.name: Authorization
parameters.description: OAuth2 access token in `Bearer {token}` format. No OAuth scope is required. Provide either this or `x-manus-api-key`, not both. See the [Open App](https://open.manus.ai/docs/v2/open-app) guide.

Message.description: A message to send to a task.

content.description: String (plain text) or array of ContentPart objects. User text is limited to approximately 5,000 estimated tokens per request; the exact character count varies by language and content. For an array, the limit applies to the combined text of all text parts; file parts do not count. Input over the limit returns InvalidArgument (HTTP 400). Each message must contain at least one non-empty visible text part or valid visible file/voice part.

connectors.description: List of connector IDs to enable for this task. Resolution order when omitted: 1) if the task belongs to a project, the project's default connectors are used; 2) otherwise, the user's default enabled connectors are used. Use [connector.list](https://open.manus.ai/docs/v2/connector.list) to get the connectors installed in your account.

enable_skills.description:
Skill IDs to enable for this task. Use [skill.list](https://open.manus.ai/docs/v2/skill.list) to retrieve available skill IDs. An empty list is treated the same as omitting this field.

- **API Key:** The user's enabled skills are loaded by default.
- **Standard OAuth client:** All App-owned skills are loaded by default, and user skills are not loaded. When a non-empty list is supplied, only App-owned IDs are used; other IDs are silently ignored.
- **Trusted client:** The user's enabled skills are loaded by default. The client's App skills are always added.

force_skills.description: Skill IDs the agent must invoke during this task. Forced skills are automatically available even if not listed in `enable_skills`. Standard OAuth clients can force only App-owned IDs; other IDs are silently ignored.

task_references.description:
IDs of existing tasks the agent can browse on demand.

- Bare 22-character task IDs only; up to 20 per request.
- On task.sendMessage, IDs are added to the task's existing references and cannot be cleared.

See the [Task references](https://open.manus.ai/docs/v2/task-references) guide.

text.description: The text content of the message. Across a ContentPart array, all text parts must contain no more than approximately 5,000 estimated tokens in total.

visibility.description: Optional. Most integrations can omit this field. A `Trusted public client` can set it to `hidden` to pass additional application context without displaying it to users. See [Hidden application context](https://open.manus.ai/docs/v2/hidden-application-context).

oneOf.title: File
oneOf.description: **Provide the file via one of: file_id, file_url, or file_data.**

file_id.description: ID of a file uploaded with [file.upload](https://open.manus.ai/docs/v2/file.upload). Up to 512 MB per file; see [Limits](https://open.manus.ai/docs/v2/file.upload#limits).

file_url.description: Publicly accessible URL to the file. Manus downloads it directly. Up to 20 MB.

file_data.description: Base64 encoded file content in the form `data:<mime_type>;base64,<encoded_content>`. Up to 20 MB after decoding.

filename.description: Display name of the file including extension (e.g., "report.pdf"). Required when using file_data; recommended for file_url.

mime_type.description: MIME type of the file (e.g., "application/pdf", "image/png"). Optional; auto-detected from filename if omitted.

visibility.description: Optional. Most integrations can omit this field. Only `visible` is supported for this content type.

oneOf.title: Voice
oneOf.description: **Provide the audio via one of: file_id, file_url, or file_data.**

file_id.description: ID of an audio file uploaded with [file.upload](https://open.manus.ai/docs/v2/file.upload). Up to 512 MB per file; see [Limits](https://open.manus.ai/docs/v2/file.upload#limits).

file_url.description: Publicly accessible URL to the audio file. Manus downloads and transcribes it. Up to 20 MB.

file_data.description: Base64 encoded audio content in the form `data:<mime_type>;base64,<encoded_content>`. Up to 20 MB after decoding.

filename.description: Display name of the audio file including extension (e.g., "recording.wav"). Required when using file_data.

mime_type.description: MIME type of the audio file (e.g., "audio/wav", "audio/mp3"). Optional; auto-detected from filename if omitted.

visibility.description: Optional. Most integrations can omit this field. Only `visible` is supported for this content type.

Task.description: Represents a task with its current status and metadata.

status.description:
Current main-agent status.

- `running` — the agent is working.
- `stopped` — the current run has stopped. Check `has_running_background_jobs` before treating the execution as complete.
- `waiting` — the agent needs user input or a confirmation.
- `error` — the task hit an unrecoverable error.

created_at.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the task was created.

updated_at.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the task was last updated.

task_type.description: Type of the task. "standard" — a regular standalone task. "project" — a task within a project. "agent_subtask" — a subtask created by an agent. Use [task.list](https://open.manus.ai/docs/v2/task.list) with `scope` to filter by task type.

share_visibility.description: Who can view the task. "private" — only the task creator. "team" — all team members. "public" — anyone with the share link.

credit_usage.description: Total credits consumed by the task. Only present when the task has consumed credits.

task_url.description: URL to view the task in the Manus webapp (e.g., https://manus.im/app/{task_id}).

created_by_api_key.description: The API key that created this task. Present when the task was created via the API; null or absent when created through the UI or other means. The name reflects the API key's current name, not a snapshot from creation time.

name.description: The current display name of the API key.

agent_profile.description: Agent profile most recently used by the task — reflects the latest turn (e.g. a [task.sendMessage](https://open.manus.ai/docs/v2/task.sendMessage) override), not just the value supplied at task creation. For backward compatibility, responses retain the legacy `manus-1.6`, `manus-1.6-lite`, or `manus-1.6-max` form even though requests should use the stable `standard`, `lite`, or `max` names. When a Max task has a thinking level selected, the level is appended, for example `manus-1.6-max-ultra`. This includes tasks whose level was chosen in the Manus web app, not only tasks created with `max-<level>`. Clients that check for Max should match the `manus-1.6-max` prefix instead of the exact value, and should tolerate new values. Omitted when this information is not available (e.g. older tasks).

has_running_background_jobs.description:
Whether non-blocking background work is still pending, queued, or running. Independent of `status`: the main agent can be stopped while background work continues.

- `true` — background work remains.
- `false` — no active background work is known.
- Omitted — unknown, typically an older task or a transient read failure; a later poll may fill it in. Do not treat omission as `false`.

See [Task status](https://open.manus.ai/docs/v2/task-lifecycle#task-status) for polling guidance.

TaskEvent.description: A task event representing a message, status change, or agent activity. Only one payload field (user_message, assistant_message, etc.) will be present, determined by the type field.

type.description: Event type. Determines which payload field is present. tool_used, plan_update, new_plan_step, and explanation are only included when verbose=true. structured_output_result appears after task completion when a structured_output_schema was provided.

timestamp.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds when this event occurred.

user_message.description: Present when type="user_message". Contains a message sent by the user.

content.description: The text content of the user's message.

message_type.description: How the message was sent. "text" for typed input, "voice" for voice input.

attachments.description: Files or images the user attached to their message.

hidden_content.description: Most integrations can ignore this field. A `Trusted public client` receives additional application context here when `verbose=true`. See [Hidden application context](https://open.manus.ai/docs/v2/hidden-application-context).

assistant_message.description: Present when type="assistant_message". Contains a response from the agent.

content.description: The text content of the agent's response.

attachments.description: Files, images, or slides the agent generated as output.

question_expectation.description: Present only for agent questions with non-empty choices. Reply with task.sendMessage, not task.confirmAction. Use the enclosing message id to identify this message; nested event_id is webhook-only and is not required for replies.

options.description: Candidate display text, not option IDs or mandatory exact-match answers. Free-text replies are allowed. Send a non-empty answer in message.content; when there are no choices, listMessages omits question_expectation (webhooks may instead use options: []).

selection_mode.description: UI selection hint: single for one candidate or multiple for several. Combine multiple selections into one readable message.content (for example, 'Please export PDF and DOCX.'); no delimiter or structured option-ID array is required. Empty or unknown upstream values normalize to single.

response_method.description: Fixed to send_message for ordinary questions, including when the upstream value is absent. This does not invoke task.confirmAction. If an unknown value is encountered, stop automatic dispatch and consult the current documentation; do not fall back to action confirmation.

delivery_kind.description: Optional display recommendation. `opening` and `progress` are primarily useful during execution and may be collapsed after the step completes. `result` is more important and should remain visible. If the value is absent or unrecognized, keep the message visible rather than hiding it.

error_message.description: Present when type="error_message". Indicates the task encountered an error.

status_update.description: Present when type="status_update". Indicates a change in the agent's processing state.

agent_status.description: The agent's current state. waiting means it needs a question answered or an action confirmed; inspect status_detail.waiting_for_event_type to choose the response endpoint.

status_detail.description: Additional details when agent_status is waiting. For action confirmations, use waiting_for_event_id with task.confirmAction. Agent questions use task.sendMessage instead.

waiting_for_event_id.description: Identifies the waiting event. For action confirmations, pass it as event_id to task.confirmAction; question replies use task.sendMessage without this parameter.

waiting_for_event_type.description: Waiting event type: messageAskUser / cascadeAskUser are questions answered with task.sendMessage; supported action types such as gmailSendAction use task.confirmAction, even without confirm_input_schema. Do not automatically confirm unrecognized types.

waiting_description.description: Human-readable description of what the agent is waiting for.

confirm_input_schema.description: JSON Schema defining the expected input format for the confirmation, if additional input is needed.

brief.description: Short summary of the current agent activity.

description.description: Detailed description of what the agent is doing.

tool_used.description: Present when type="tool_used". Tool events normally require verbose=true. A confirmation target can be fetched with verbose=true and start_event_id=waiting_for_event_id only when the target projects to tool_used. Configuration and OAuth targets do not; attempting this lookup for them returns Event not found.

tool.description: Name of the tool that was used (e.g., "browser", "code_executor").

action_id.description: Unique identifier for this tool action.

status.description: Tool projection status. pending_confirmation means the operation has not executed and is waiting for task.confirmAction, but some confirmation targets such as Gmail and Calendar retain success while waiting. Determine confirmation state from agent_status=waiting and waiting_for_event_id, not from this field alone.

brief.description: Short summary of the tool action.

description.description: Detailed description of what the tool did.

message.description: Human-readable display summary for the tool invocation. This is not the structured tool input.

action.description: Human-readable label describing the tool action. The action may still be awaiting confirmation.

param.description: Optional human-readable detail shown with the action. This is not the structured tool input; use tool_used.params for structured parameters.

params.description: Structured parameters supplied to the tool. Returned when the confirmation target is fetched with verbose=true and start_event_id=waiting_for_event_id, or when that target and its waiting status are returned on the same page. Use them to review the proposed operation; do not submit them directly as task.confirmAction input.

result.description: Optional structured tool result used as confirmation context for result-driven operations, such as selecting an account or publishing prepared media. Returned under the same conditions as params.

plan_update.description: Present when type="plan_update" (verbose=true only). A full snapshot of the agent's current execution plan.

steps.description: All steps in the current plan with their statuses.

status.description: Current status of this plan step.

started_at.description: Unix timestamp when this step started. Null if not yet started.

end_at.description: Unix timestamp when this step finished. Null if not yet completed.

new_plan_step.description: Present when type="new_plan_step" (verbose=true only). A new step was added to the plan.

step_id.description: Unique identifier for the new plan step.

title.description: Description of the new plan step.

explanation.description: Present when type="explanation" (verbose=true only). The agent's internal reasoning or thought process.

content.description: The agent's explanation of its reasoning or approach.

structured_output_result.description: Present when type="structured_output_result". Contains the extracted structured data. Appears after the status_update (stopped) event when the task was created with a structured_output_schema.

success.description: Whether the agent produced a meaningful result. When false, value contains schema-conforming defaults and error explains what happened.

value.description: The extracted value conforming to the schema provided in structured_output_schema. Always present and valid, even when success is false — see [zero-value rules](https://open.manus.ai/docs/v2/structured-output#when-success-is-false).

error.description: Error description when success is false. Null when success is true.

TaskAttachment.description: A file or media attachment in a task message.

type.description:
Type of attachment.

- `image` — image.
- `file` — document.
- `voice` — audio recording.
- `slides` — presentation slides.

filename.description: Display name of the attachment file.

url.description: URL to download the attachment content.

path.description: Optional execution-environment path referenced by the message body. Match it to a Markdown link or image destination, then use url to download the attachment. This path is not itself downloadable.

file_uid.description: Stable identifier of the backing output file. Present with `version_uid` when the attachment has a download URL and file identity. See [Attachments](https://open.manus.ai/docs/v2/attachments#file-paths).

version_uid.description: Stable identifier of the backing output file version. Present with `file_uid`. See [Attachments](https://open.manus.ai/docs/v2/attachments#file-paths).

Project.description: A project for organizing tasks with shared instructions.

created_at.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the project was created.

instruction.description: Default instruction applied to all tasks in this project.

Skill.description: A skill that extends the agent's capabilities.

id.description: Unique identifier for the skill. Use this in enable_skills or force_skills when creating tasks.

description.description: What the skill does and when it's useful.

owner_type.description:
Who owns the skill.

- `personal` — user-created skill.
- `official` — built-in system skill.
- `team` — team-shared skill.
- `project` — project-specific skill.
- `app` — private skill owned by an Open App.

creator_info.description: Information about who created the skill.

user_id.description: User ID of the skill creator.

name.description: Display name of the skill creator.

created_at.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the skill was created.

updated_at.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the skill was last updated.

Agent.description: A custom agent with its own identity (nickname and description) that can be customized for specific use cases. See the [Agents](https://open.manus.ai/docs/v2/agents-overview) guide.

id.description: Unique identifier for the agent. Use this as `agent_id` in [task.list](https://open.manus.ai/docs/v2/task.list) (with `scope=agent_subtask`) to view this agent's subtasks.

task_id.description: The agent's main task, which is its persistent conversation thread. Pass it as `task_id` to [task.sendMessage](https://open.manus.ai/docs/v2/task.sendMessage) to talk to the agent, or to [task.listMessages](https://open.manus.ai/docs/v2/task.listMessages) to read the conversation. For the IM agent, the shortcut `agent-default-main_task` resolves to this value.

nickname.description: Display name of the agent. Can be updated via [agent.update](https://open.manus.ai/docs/v2/agent.update).

about.description: Description or bio of the agent explaining its purpose and specialization. Can be updated via [agent.update](https://open.manus.ai/docs/v2/agent.update).

ArtifactSource.description: Credential attributable to the artifact's creation task. Omitted when no API key or OAuth client ID is available, including UI-created tasks and API-created tasks without recorded credential IDs.

kind.description: Credential type that created the source task.

oauth_client_id.description: Open App client ID. Present when kind is oauth_client.

api_key_id.description: API key ID. Present when kind is api_key.

name.description: Current credential display name when available.

Artifact.description: A generated task artifact indexed by Manus Library.

task_title.description: Current title of the task that produced the artifact.

filename.description: Physical filename, including its extension when available.

display_name.description: User-facing artifact name shown in Manus Library.

type.description: Library category, as used by the `type` filter. Based on the indexed file type and extension. See [Artifact categories](https://open.manus.ai/docs/v2/artifacts#artifact-categories).

content_type.description: MIME type inferred from the filename when available.

url.description: Download or site URL when the artifact has a public API-consumable URL.

cover_image.description: Cover or preview image URL when available.

favorite.description: Whether the user favorited the artifact in Manus Library.

platform_type.description:
WebDev platform.

- `1` — Web.
- `2` — Mobile.
- `3` — Game.

Treat other values as unknown.

logo.description: WebDev application logo. Present for mobile WebDev artifacts when available.

resource_uri.description: Addon Resource identity. Returned instead of treating an internal resource URI as a download URL.

source.description: Credential attributable to the producing task. Omitted when no API key or OAuth client ID is available; omission does not imply that the task was created in the UI.

File.description: Basic file information returned in lists and upload responses.

id.description: Unique identifier for the file. Use this as file_id when attaching to tasks.

status.description: File status. "pending" — waiting for upload. "uploaded" — ready to use. "deleted" — file has been deleted. "error" — upload failed.

created_at.description: Unix timestamp in seconds when the file record was created, encoded as a decimal string.

FileDetail.description: Full file information returned by file.detail.

status.description: File status. "pending" — waiting for upload. "uploaded" — ready to use. "deleted" — file has been deleted. "error" — upload failed.

created_at.description: Unix timestamp in seconds when the file record was created, encoded as a decimal string.

bytes.description: File size in bytes, encoded as a decimal string. May be "0" before the upload is confirmed.

expires_at.description: Unix timestamp in seconds when the file expires, encoded as a decimal string.

error_message.description: Error description if the file status is "error".

Webhook.description: A webhook subscription for receiving task event notifications.

url.description: The endpoint URL receiving webhook POST notifications.

created_at.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the webhook was created.

BrowserClient.description: An online browser client connected to the user's account.

client_id.description: Unique identifier for the browser client.

client_name.description: Display name of the browser client.

id.description: Unique identifier for the connector. Use this as the connector ID when creating tasks.

type.description: Connector type. "builtin" — built-in connector provided by Manus. "byok" — bring-your-own-key connector. "mcp" — MCP (Model Context Protocol) connector.

description.description: Human-readable description of the connector's functionality.

AvailableCredits.description: Credit balance, subscription period, and refresh information for the authenticated caller. All credit fields are 32-bit integers in credit points. `total_credits` is the authoritative spendable balance — see the field descriptions for how it is composed.

total_credits.description: Total available credits — the actual spendable wallet balance. Equals `free_credits + periodic_credits + addon_credits + event_credits + refresh_credits`, minus team overflow credits, where `periodic_credits` and `addon_credits` are counted as 0 when the membership has lapsed and `event_credits` is 0 when no event is active. Always treat this as the single authoritative value for how many credits can be spent.

free_credits.description: Free credits unrelated to any subscription, such as sign-up gifts and system grants.

periodic_credits.description: Remaining periodic subscription credits issued in the current billing cycle and not yet spent. Returns 0 when the membership has lapsed.

addon_credits.description: Remaining add-on / credit-pack credits that were purchased separately and do not reset with the subscription cycle. In team scenarios this already accounts for deducted-but-unpaid overflow credits.

pro_monthly_credits.description: VIP monthly periodic-credit quota — how many periodic credits the current membership tier issues each month. This is a quota, not a current balance. 0 for non-VIP accounts.

event_credits.description: Remaining event (live event) credits. Returns the real value only while the account's bound campaign is still active; otherwise 0.

refresh_credits.description: Remaining auto-refresh credits accumulated on the account (daily/weekly) and not yet spent.

max_refresh_credits.description: Amount granted by a single refresh — the cap the next auto-refresh will issue. Only present for personal accounts; 0 for team accounts.

next_refresh_time.description: Time of the next refresh as a Unix timestamp in seconds (UTC). Only present for personal accounts; 0 when there is no upcoming refresh.

refresh_interval.description: Refresh cadence: `daily` or `weekly`. Empty string when there is no refresh schedule (e.g., team accounts).

current_period_end.description: Subscription period end as a Unix timestamp in seconds (UTC). Returns 0 when no subscription period is returned; an expired subscription may return a timestamp in the past. Temporary event membership does not change this value.

UsageRecord.description: A credit change record at session granularity. Covers consumption, refunds, subscription grants, and admin adjustments.

task_id.description: The task (session) ID this change is associated with.

title.description: The task title. Returns "Deleted conversation" if the session has been deleted.

credits.description: Credit change amount. Negative values represent consumption; positive values represent refunds or subscription/admin grants.

created_at.description: Time of the most recent change as a Unix timestamp in seconds.

type.description:
Change type:

- `cost` — credit consumption (task usage or admin deduction)
- `refund` — credit returned after consumption (e.g., task failure rollback)
- `grant` — credits gained (subscription grant, upgrade bonus, recurring issuance, credit pack purchase, admin compensation)

collaborate_infos.description: Per-collaborator credit breakdown for team tasks. Empty for personal tasks.

credits.description: Credits attributed to this collaborator for the task.

date.description: Date as a Unix timestamp in seconds, representing 00:00:00 of that day.

credits.description: Total credits consumed on this day.

TeamUsageLog.description: Per-user aggregated task count and credit consumption over the requested range. One row per team member.

task_count.description: Number of tasks the member created within the requested range.

credits.description: Total credits consumed by this user within the requested range.

WebsiteCheckpoint.description: A snapshot of a website (backed by a git commit).

version_id.description: Unique checkpoint version ID (the underlying git commit hash).

message.description: Checkpoint description — the commit message written when the checkpoint was saved.

status.description: Whether the checkpoint itself was generated successfully. This is independent of publish state — use `published_version_id` from `website.listCheckpoints` to identify the version currently live.

ErrorResponse.description: Standard error response format returned when a request fails.

request_id.description: Unique identifier for this API request, useful for debugging with support.

message.description: Human-readable error description explaining what went wrong.
